Accounting trap

A customer pays $120 today. How much is revenue?

Most people get this wrong in interviews.

The question

On Dec 1, a customer prepays $120 for a 12-month subscription. Year ends Dec 31. Revenue this year?

A$120
B$0
C$10
D$60

Pick one, then swipe.

Answer
C. $10

You only earn revenue as you deliver. One month of service = $120 ÷ 12.

Where's the rest?
+$120
Cashit all came in on Dec 1
$10
Revenue1 month delivered
$110
Deferred revenuea liability: 11 months still owed

Curveball

Why is the $110 a liability and not good news?

Because you still owe the customer 11 months of service. If you never deliver, you give the money back.

Cash up, revenue barely moves. Did you pick A? 👇
